analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump, a Nemotron Super body-size description, and a JSON-with-tools behavior note. The two supplied units (base lines 802-1610) lie outside the changed base ranges [3], [128-130], [528], [540-541], so I saw only the unchanged surrounding GLM, calibration, deadline and MTP prose. The patch excerpt is incomplete (patch_excerpt_complete=false) and the changed hunks are not in my units. No executable code, configuration or control changes are visible, so I found no concrete security regression and no invalidated assumption for T-041 or other cited threats.

Two items for later passes to check against actual code, neither a finding here:
1. The doc says the Nemotron Super `maximumEncodedBodyBytes` rose from 8 MiB to 40 MiB and now returns `media_too_large`. If the implementation changed accordingly, that raises memory and DoS exposure on TB-002 and TB-007. Admission still goes through the shared media-memory budget and returns a 503, per the doc. That implementation is not in the supplied evidence.
2. The note that a JSON response format may come with tools, with a tool-calling turn returning its calls unvalidated, could weaken structured-output validation. That depends on the code.

The unchanged prefix-cache sections (the Nemotron paragraph at head 530-532 on coordinator text prefix reuse partitioned by authenticated cache scope) are consistent with the T-041 scoping model. I did not verify any code claim.
